absent: Remainder of guest abort handling after nested resolution and dispatch among guest-memory, protected and user paths.
Encodings of protection bits, fault-status codes, syndrome fields and nested level representation.
Stage-2 table primitives for map, relax, young-marking and hypervisor share, donate and revoke operations.
Memcache provisioning, fault-lock implementation, invalidation sequencing and source-read scope.
Tag sanitisation, transparent-huge promotion, cacheable PFNMAP support test and dirty-logging mechanics.

findings.text: Fault descriptor aggregates the faulting vCPU, the faulting intermediate address, an optional nested translation result, the covering memory slot reference, and the host virtual address. It is shared read-only across guest-memory and user-memory abort handling.

VMA-derived fault state carries an invalidation sequence sample, host mapping size and ceiling, VMA flags, resolved guest and host frames with optional page reference, and booleans for device nature, tag permission, cacheability, writability and forced non-cacheable treatment.

Nested permission adjustment intersects requested protection with readability, writability and exception-level executability reported by the nested translation, while retaining a nested level encoding. Faults therefore cannot gain rights denied by nested tables.

Guest-memory fault handling resolves the guest frame from nested output when present otherwise from fault address, obtains a backing page, starts from readable protection extended for writable slots and for instruction or DIC-capable cases, constrains by nested rights, then under fault protection either relaxes an existing entry or installs a fresh single-page entry and marks writable success dirty.

Protected-hypervisor memory fault handling reserves hypervisor memcache and locked-memory accounting, pins exactly one host page for write with poison handling, rejects unsuitable file-backed pages, then under exclusive MMU protection installs a single full-access page mapping and unwinds pin and accounting on failure.

Stage-2 install service tracks every range in a table-local collection. Protected VMs accept only single-page full-access installs with distinct contention reporting; other VMs accept page or larger block sizes, replace overlapping tracked ranges, and delegate sharing to the hypervisor before recording frames and cacheability.

Range revocation walks tracked mappings overlapping a half-open interval with a next-pointer-safe iterator, requests hypervisor revocation per entry, then removes and frees each tracker. Iteration covers the inclusive end derived from end minus one.

Host mapping granularity starts from logging state and VMA-reported size, steps down through larger block levels unless slot and host address support huge stage-2 use, then clamps to nested translation size when shadowing and aligns the result to a supported host size, warning on unexpected sizes.

VMA capture under host address-space read protection records mapping size, aligned guest frame, tag permission, flags and cacheability plus an invalidation sequence sample, failing when no VMA covers the host address. Canonical guest frame for nested faults derives from nested output aligned to the chosen size.

Pinning combines VMA capture with fault-in of the canonical frame using write intent on write faults, signals poison distinctly without error propagation, rejects other error frames, and classifies struct-page-less PFN or mixed mappings as device with cacheability checks and forced non-cacheable treatment where required.

Protection derivation rejects execution on forced non-cacheable mappings, returns exclusive-atomic faults to the guest, starts readable with conditional write for device or non-logged or write cases, applies nested constraints, adds execution for instruction or DIC-host cases with nested execution filtering, selects non-cacheable versus device treatment from VMA permission, and validates tag permission on relevant tag-enabled faults.

Stage-2 map under fault protection abandons on invalidation race, considers permission-fault granule, upgrades single-page requests via granule or transparent-huge promotion when a larger ceiling allows, sanitises tags for tag-enabled cacheable installs, relaxes when size matches the fault granule otherwise installs anew, then releases the page and marks the canonical aligned range dirty on writable success.

User-memory abort ensures memcache availability for translation faults and for logging or protected-hypervisor permission faults, then executes pin, protection derivation and map stages, releasing the page if protection derivation fails.

Stage-2 installs sample the MMU invalidation sequence before acquiring fault protection and abandon on sequence change, with ordering against invalidation completion. Page release and unlock occur together after map or relax attempts.

Protected table install requires exclusive MMU protection held by the caller and asserted on entry, while access-flag handling takes only shared MMU protection around young-marking. Host VMA lookup and page pinning hold host address-space read protection only across the lookup or pin.
Access-flag faults emit a trace record and mark the stage-2 entry young for the faulting address using shared walk semantics.

Host ownership of synchronous external aborts holds when RAS extension support is absent, when a hypervisor-context data abort carries virtual-control indication outside nested context, or when a table-walk abort is identifiable as stage-2 by fault code plus first-stage-walk indication.

Synchronous external abort service first offers the event to platform firmware handling with interrupts enabled, injects a virtual error when host-owned or when userspace exit is disabled, otherwise reports a masked syndrome plus guest virtual and physical addresses through a dedicated exit reason.

Guest abort entry diverts external aborts early, validates the fault address, enforces IPA limits with size-fault injection beyond the sanitised range and error injection in the gap to the configured range, traces the fault, rejects unsupported fault-status codes, and acquires source-read protection before nested resolution.

Stage-2 fault disposition branches on permission versus translation kind: permission faults favour in-place relaxation without fresh allocation except for logging-driven collapse or protected block handling, while translation faults require memcache provisioning and fresh install; invalidation or mapping contention normalises to benign success.
External-abort disposition proceeds from firmware claim to host-owned versus guest-owned determination and then to virtual-error injection versus userspace exit with address-validity signalling.

Hazards include simultaneous write and execution indications, missing host VMA, unexpected mapping size, poisoned host pages, file-backed pages unsuitable for protected pinning, cacheable PFN mappings lacking required hardware support, execution on non-cacheable memory, unexpected overlapping protected mappings, and unsupported fault-status codes.
Protected VMs use single-page full read-write-execute stage-2 entries; non-protected installs allow page or block granularity with cacheability recorded from device or non-cacheable attributes.

Userspace synchronous-error exit preserves class, length, validity, async, capture, write and fault-status fields in the syndrome plus tag-error bits when RAS is present, with separate physical-address validity and omission of virtual address on not-valid indication.
